notes:
**The count badge on every finding now names what it counted.**

A finding that said "3,165 images use JPEG/PNG instead of a modern format"
carried a badge reading "3165 pages" — on a site of 659. Three findings in one
report claimed more pages than the whole crawl, and two contradicted their own
body text a line below. The titles were right all along; the badge overrode them
in the HTML report, the Markdown export and the PDF, because a finding had no
way to say whether it was counting pages, images, links, colour groups or AI
crawlers. Fifty-six checks now say, and a gate holds every badge to the title it
sits above.

**The action plan says when it is not showing everything.**

The plan sequences the forty highest-priority items. On a report with more than
that, the cover promised fifty items and the plan printed forty with nothing
saying why. It now says how many are sequenced, out of how many, and where the
rest are.

**"Pages crawled" no longer means two different things in one report.**

The cover counts every URL fetched; the AI-substitution section counted the ones
that returned readable HTML, and called both "pages crawled". One report said
659 on its cover and 640 nine pages later. Both numbers were right and the
phrase was doing two jobs.

**Four links to one phone number are reported as one phone number.**

Most sites publish one number in a template, so it appears on every page. Docket
counted the links: "4 tel: links carry a national number... for example
03709000100", where that was the only number on the site. The fix read as four
edits rather than one line of a template.

**An archive page is no longer told how many entries it has.**

"Each one lists only an entry or two" was a sentence, not a measurement. The
page that prompted this lists four. It now reports its word count, which is the
number the check actually has.

**The share of the site a crawl read is printed next to what it read.**

"found at least 1,034 more it did not reach — about 4% of the site" put the
percentage after the wrong half of the sentence. Four per cent was what Docket
read; the 1,034 it missed were the other 96%.
